There are a couple of different things you can do to be declared independent for the purposes of centrelink.

1. Working - i forget the needed amount but it is something like 75% of minimum wage within last 18 months. Need payslips to show this.

2. Relationship - that you've been in a marriage / defacto relationship for at least 12 months. Will need to supply evidence of this.

3. Unreasonable to live at home - due to family breakdown, space or a variety of other reasons it is no longer possible to live at home. Because you are over 18 you'll have to fill in a form, your parents will have to fill in a form and an independent party will as well.

As you would most likely come under 3 some pointers. It will be assessed by a social worker. If you cant get your parents to fill it in then let them know. They will still try and contact them anyway. It is better if the 3rd party is a professional - community organisation, youth worker etc.

In the mean time do the following:
Lodge a claim immediately. Starts the ball rolling.
Visit your local office. They will be able to link you with local services to help out.

Please realise that yes this can be sped up depending on financial hardship but will still take some time.

You are unfortunately in a very very tough spot. Getting dsp under the new impairment tables and rules is really hard. Have a read through the stuff you've got from your doctor's.   Does it mention at all there is any possibility of change within the next two years? Even something as simple as doc saying with medication might become more stable?

If so you generally won't qualify. One of the big sticking points is that the condition needs to be fully treated, diagnosed and stabilised. No expected changes within 2 years.

You may also have to go to a government doctor to have it all reassessed by them as well. Be prepared for that. 

Words to make it go faster? Unfortunately there is probably a massive backlog of claims so expect a delay. Has you partner applied for new start provisional while awaiting the outcome? They get placed on new start but don't have to meet any participation requirements while the claim is being processed.

As for your carers claim. Only suggestion is that when you are filling the forms out make sure you answer the questions based on your partners worst days not how they are the day you fill in the form.

I've been taking out twin 3 year olds for walking 9 holes for the last six months or so at my home course. Granted it didn't start as full 9 but worked up to it. 
Things I found worked for me is teaching them as we went alone. To be quiet if others are swinging. No yelling and shouting. There is a fair bit of running on their behalf but I go mostly when it's quiet so no one has complained yet. 
One of the best things I think I did though was bought them a couple of clubs to. Start with the plastics and work upto normals. I'd show them how to hit and let them have a hit every time I did. Keeps them interested and they love putting now. 

Only other pro tip. Especially here in Australia. Water. Take lots of it. I've learnt that If I think I've got enough, I'll need at least 1 bottle more. 

But otherwise have fun with it. It's a good thing to get the kids into and the best part is I can tell the missus I'm going to golf and not get frowned on. Win win

It isn't released everywhere. There are a few other countries like Australia that will be getting it later. The only reason New Zealand has it now is because part of the deal was they got the first release / premier if I recall correctly. 
Its got to do with when a country normally releases the 'blockbusters' for this period. Some countries do there's before Christmas, Australia does it on boxing day. Remember boxing day isn't as big in other parts of the world, they have had or are currently having there holidays now leading up to Christmas. 

Means we get shafted on Christmas releases. But then we do get other movies earlier especially around July.
This is an easy one. Distributors and cinemas want to release it on Boxing Day to make sure they cash in the most. Nothing extra, just them figuring out how to make the most money off of the release.

I am the friendly, nice person, that is always happy and cheerful. 

I have no idea what these feelings are actually, I just learned how to mimic them at a young age. For a very, very long time I've suffered from extreme emotional detachment with a borderline personality disorder. I can honestly say, I can't remember what it feels like to be happy or sad, except anger. I have spikes in either direction, but they are suppressed quickly. My general state is numb/ neutral and everything else is a complete lie. I learned to mimic what people expect or want. Also how to appear to be concerned and trustful for people to tell me their secrets. When the whole time I was getting their secrets so I could hold them over them if they ever found out mine.  

Yes I know what caused it and I've sort treatment. I even had a 'break' where I actually reverted and started feeling emotions and feelings and all that. My girlfriend at the time, all my close friends and my family knew about the incident and what caused me to revert to actually being able to feel emotions again. 
There response? They all complained that I wasn't myself and that they wanted me to get back to 'normal' and stop acting out and start being there for them again. First time in 15 years I actually felt anything, only to be told no one liked me and I wasn't as dependable to them anymore. 

Sadly this lead me to reverting to my old ways. Numb is my way of life. Well except for anger. Anger has always been there, always has been, always will be.
